newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to aim East Europe aid at preparing new members.
newsitem.headline: EU to aim East Europe aid at preparing new members.

text.p: The European Union on Wednesday turned its fragmented aid programme for eastern Europe into a super-fund aimed at getting formerly communist countries ready for EU membership.

In a move that shifts much of the decision-making on development spending from the region to Brussels, the European Commission said it was completely revamping its multi-billion dollar PHARE programme.
PHARE was set up after the fall of the Berlin Wall to help the former communist countries bring their command economies into line with the rest of Europe's free enterprise system.
Grants reached 4.2 billion European currency units ($4.83 billion) between 1990 and 1994. A further 6.7 billion Ecus are budgeted for 1995-99.

Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Bulgaria, Romania, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Albania, Bosnia and the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia are eligible. All but the last three have been promised eventual EU membership.
Commission officials said the programme to date had been driven by requests from the countries, resulting in a plethora of small projects, many run by outside consultants and not all run efficiently.

Under the new system, which will start immediately, the EU will draw up national programmes with the 10 countries being offered membership. The money will be aimed directly at preparing the countries to join the EU.
"PHARE must from now on concentrate on the real priorities," External Affairs Commissioner Hans van den Broek said in a statement.
Albania, Macedonia and Bosnia would have different programmes, similar to what already exists.

The Commission said some 30 percent of PHARE money would now be spent on strengthening democratic institutions in the 10 applicant countries and 7O percent to help the countries finance investments aimed at improving business and infrastructure
Projects would be bigger and more directly run. "We will be relying less on consultants," one Commission source said.
Officials said current projects would be phased out and the new ones phased in to avoid pulling the plug on some existing programmes. But some money allocated for programmes previously would be lost.
Between 1990 and 1994 some 2.3 billion Ecus in PHARE funds were allocated for projects but did not result in formal contracts, mainly because of bureaucracy.
Although many contracts would now be signed and much of the money would be re-directed to similar projects, officials said some of it was in danger of simply being lost to the recipients.
